checked.claim: Contraband destroys a student's item and tells nobody whose it was
checked.why: The code is as cited: destroyItemEffect deletes and pushes one line with the item's name only, and no `tell` (call-effects.mjs:1355-1362); drpgDespairCall has no listener (one callAll, calls.mjs:548). But the failure scenario overstates it: the public card is a public announcement, which raises a notice on every player's browser (popup.mjs:1255-1262, "public announcements - no whisper list at all; that IS an announcement", tone `fear`, calls.mjs:533), so the owner does read that their Crowbar was destroyed at the moment it happens, unless two people carry items of the same name; and the item's own picker labels are a GM's ("carried by", call-pickers.mjs:551-552). No rule or paper was found that asks for a private notice to the owner, and an item on a body (CALL-14, call-pickers.mjs:527-535) has nobody to tell. What remains is a missing owner's notice when names repeat: a text-and-ux nit, not wrong behaviour in a particular situation.

checked.claim: Two GMs writing a seal or a restriction at once keep only one, and restrict answers true whatever was written
checked.why: The race half holds on reading: sealRoom and restrict read the world setting from this browser's copy, change one entry and set the whole value (call-world.mjs:65-69, 134-139), writeWorld has no serial step and no primary hand-off (202-207), and Despair Calls are applied on the buying GM's browser (calls.mjs:416-419 refuses only players; applyCall runs locally at 481-483), with two Monokumas on two GMs a supported case (calls.mjs:405-406). No other writer of either setting serialises it (grep: passages-gm.mjs:796 also calls sealRoom). The interleaving was not measured; it needs two GM writes within one round trip, so minor holds. The second half does not hold on a real road: writeWorld answers null only for a non-GM (204), and every caller of restrict is a Despair effect on a GM's browser; a failed game.settings.set throws out of restrict into applyCall, which marks the Call failed and refunds, so a Silence or a Chain is not announced when nothing was written. That half is refuted; the finding's title claim stands.
